title: Jetpack burst: stabilize short-session TTFT and tokens/sec across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Nora Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated enterprise VPC + Private on-prem customer) reported intermittent, short-duration bursts of extremely elevated TTFT and simultaneous drop in tokens/sec for short sessions (<200 tokens). The pattern started 2025-02-14 after a prioritized kernel selector heuristic change that aimed to favor new quantized kernels under medium batch sizes. Impact: median TTFT for short sessions jumped from ~55ms to ~310ms during bursts; aggregate tokens/sec fell ~40% for affected workers. Scope: affects mixed-variant traffic (fp16 + int8 switchover), short-session traffic, and appears across regions and deployment modes.
steps_taken: 2025-02-15 02:10 UTC - Triage: attached customer traces, reproduced with synthetic client hitting short-session workload with 80% small prompts, 20% long contexts
Telemetry: identified correlation between kernel fallback events and upstream scheduler reordering; frequent KV cache invalidations observed when worker switched active contexts

Root cause hypothesis: aggressive kernel heuristic caused intermittent fallback to generic kernel that has poor per-token performance for small sequence lengths; scheduler mis-ranked warmup priority causing prefetch storms and KV cache evictions leading to repeated re-warmups

Mitigations deployed: temporarily pinned vulnerable model variants to stable kernel family (hotpatch to runtime-1.22), enabled conservative scheduler weights for warmup traffic in hosted region us-west-2
Load tests: synthetic ramp validated pin reduces median TTFT to ~70ms in controlled runs; tokens/sec recovered to within 10% of baseline
comments: 2025-02-15 Nora P: Initial customer escalation received from Enterprise Ops (ticket #C-8124). Repro script created and shared in #prod-ttft. Marked as P0 due to multiple paid customers affected.
2025-02-16 Marcus L: Confirmed reproduction on staging with mixed quantized model set. Observed kernel selection logs show ~23% fallback rate during bursts. Opened prototype hotpatch branch.
2025-02-17 QA (Elena G): Stress test 12x clients for 30m. Pin to stable kernel passes but exposes an unrelated memory fragmentation leak on int8 path — logged as ENG-478203 (follow-up).
2025-02-18 Marcus L: Deployed emergency pin to canary pool (10% traffic) in hosted and Dedicated test clusters. Monitoring dashboards show 65% reduction in burst magnitude on canaries.

2025-02-20 Incident review: decision to roll out scheduler weight tweak + hedged-warmstart reserve bucket to reduce KV eviction. Trade-off: slight increase in idle memory footprint for reserve bucket but expected to reduce re-warm CPU cost.
2025-02-22 Nora P: Customer communications drafted and sent for affected accounts with ETA for full rollout (see incident doc).
acceptance_criteria: Baseline median TTFT for short sessions returns to <=90ms in production across hosted/dedicated/private for 72h post-rollout
Aggregate tokens/sec for short-session workload recovers to within 15% of historical baseline during peak hours
No regression observed in long-context throughput or tail latency (P95/P99 unchanged within +/-5%)
Canary rollout to 20% traffic for 24h with zero new customer escalations before global rollout
next_steps: Complete runtime PR for scheduler-weight-adjust and reserve-bucket hedging (PR referenced above) and get security sign-off for canary deployment
Coordinate with Dedicated ops to schedule weekend rollout for on-prem/private where automated hotpatch isn't available
Create long-term plan: add model-variant-aware kernel bench matrix to CI and a regression alert tied to small-session TTFT delta
Postmortem: write-action items and link to roadmap item for kernel selection rework (runtime-1.24)
Inform Sales/CS teams when Dedicated/private rollouts are scheduled so they can notify impacted customers
